{{nihongo|'''Akaruhimenomikoto Shrine'''|赤留比売命神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Settsu Province]].

'''Akahirume-no-Mikoto Shrine''' (あかるひめのみことじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located in {{ill|Hirano-higashi|Q88982379|qid=Q88982379}}, {{ill|Hirano-ku, Osaka|Q861256|qid=Q861256}}, {{ill|Osaka|Q35765|qid=Q35765}}.

It enshrines {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Akahirume-no-Mikoto}} as its {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=principal deity}}. Because it is an {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}-listed {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=shrine}} (a {{ill|kokuheisha|Q11452104|qid=Q11452104}} under the ritsuryō system), it is believed to have already existed by the mid-{{ill|Heian period|Q193292|qid=Q193292}}<ref>{{Cite web|Japanese book|title=26. Akahirume-no-Mikoto Shrine |url=https://www.city.osaka.lg.jp/kensetsu/page/0000009222.html |website=Osaka City |access-date=2023-04-22 |language=ja}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|Japanese book|title=Akahirume-no-Mikoto Shrine (Sanjūbu Shrine) |url=https://www.city.osaka.lg.jp/hirano/page/0000210304.html |website=Osaka City |access-date=2023-04-22 |language=ja}}</ref>.

=== History ===
In the medieval period, it was called “Sanjūbu Shrine” (三十歩神社). There are various theories regarding the origin of the name Sanjūbu Shrine.

One theory holds that during the {{ill|Ōei|Q1193078|qid=Q1193078}} era of the {{ill|Muromachi period|Q334845|qid=Q334845}}, there was a {{ill|Drought|Q43059|qid=Q43059}}, and when {{ill|Rainmaking (ritual)|Q477738|qid=Q477738}} rituals were performed, thirty copies of the {{ill|Lotus Sutra|Q861212|qid=Q861212}} were chanted, resulting in divine efficacy. Another theory states that the shrine grounds at the time measured thirty steps in size.

Today, it is a {{ill|Setsumatsusha|Q1071160|qid=Q1071160|lt=末社}} of {{ill|Kumata Shrine|Q11523763|qid=Q11523763}}, but it was formerly a subsidiary shrine of {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|Q705949|qid=Q705949}}<ref>{{Cite web|Japanese book|title=Album of Heisei 25 |url=https://kumata.jp/h25album |website=Kumata Shrine |date=2016-07-28 |access-date=2023-04-22 |language=ja |last=Shrine Office}}</ref>.
